headline_marked: Govt to set up [[first free trade zones]] near Chattogram and Cox's Bazar ports
headline: Govt to set up first free trade zones near Chattogram and Cox's Bazar ports
summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the establishment of two zones on 600 acres to boost foreign investment and international trade.
details: The Bangladesh government is taking steps to establish the country's first two free trade zones near the Matarbari seaport in Cox's Bazar and the Chattogram Port.
Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani stated that the initiative aims to accelerate economic growth, expand international trade, and attract more foreign investment.
The plan involves establishing these zones on approximately 600 acres of land, with 300 acres allocated for Matarbari and the remaining 300 acres near Chattogram Port.
Detailed project plans, investment structures, and operational modalities will be finalized in the next phase of the project.

Additionally, the government gave in-principle approval for a development and land lease agreement with Bangladesh CEIZ Company Ltd for the Chinese Economic and Industrial Zone (CEIZ) in Anwara, Chattogram.
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council has approved a Tk 4,189 crore project to develop supporting infrastructure for the CEIZ in Anwara.
Of the total cost for the CEIZ infrastructure, Tk 1,722 crore will be provided by government funds and Tk 2,467 crore will be financed through a Preferential Buyer's Credit loan from China.
caption:
Bangladesh is getting its first-ever free trade zones to supercharge international trade and foreign investment.

The Bangladesh government is taking steps to establish the country's first two free trade zones near the Matarbari seaport in Cox's Bazar and the Chattogram Port.

Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani stated that the initiative aims to accelerate economic growth, expand international trade, and attract more foreign investment.

The plan involves establishing these zones on approximately 600 acres of land, with 300 acres allocated for Matarbari and the remaining 300 acres near Chattogram Port.

Detailed project plans, investment structures, and operational modalities will be finalized in the next phase of the project.

Additionally, the government gave in-principle approval for a development and land lease agreement with Bangladesh CEIZ Company Ltd for the Chinese Economic and Industrial Zone (CEIZ) in Anwara, Chattogram.

The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council has approved a Tk 4,189 crore project to develop supporting infrastructure for the CEIZ in Anwara.

Of the total cost for the CEIZ infrastructure, Tk 1,722 crore will be provided by government funds and Tk 2,467 crore will be financed through a Preferential Buyer's Credit loan from China.

headline: 4 children die as measles outbreak spreads in Bangladesh
summary: 111 new cases detected in 24 hours as the national death toll from confirmed and suspected cases climbs.
details: Four children with measles symptoms died in Bangladesh over the last 24 hours, while 111 more people were diagnosed with the highly infectious disease.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 93 people have died of confirmed measles nationwide since March 15.
An additional 568 people are suspected to have died with measles symptoms, bringing the total suspected death toll significantly higher.
The Dhaka Division has seen the highest number of suspected deaths with 239, followed by Rajshahi with 87 deaths.
In a single 24-hour period, 966 people visited hospitals with measles symptoms, with 872 of them requiring admission.
Dhaka recorded the highest number of hospital admissions at 315, while Rangpur recorded the lowest at 25.
Since the start of the outbreak, Bangladesh has confirmed 10,634 cases of measles, but the suspected caseload is estimated to be as high as 88,895.
